name: MMA Crossover Strategy
description: A rules-based observation guide for BJJ students comparing grappling exchanges with sanctioned MMA.
summary: Study how MMA scoring, grounded-fighter rules and fence restrictions change the context of familiar grappling positions.
overview: A BJJ position name does not translate directly into an MMA score. The ABC judging clarification evaluates productive offense and expressly distinguishes it from merely holding a position. Its rules also define grounded-fighter status and distinguish contact with the fence from grabbing it. These are useful starting questions when observing an MMA exchange.

fits: You can recognize BJJ positions but want to understand why a similar-looking MMA exchange has different tactical constraints.
consider_alternative_if: For grappling without strikes, use No-Gi Competition Approach and its event-specific rules comparison.

includes: The difference between occupying a position and producing the offense discussed in MMA judging criteria.
Rules defining a grounded fighter and restricting fence grabs.
limits: The selected ABC documents concern their stated MMA rules; amateur and commission-specific provisions require their own checks.
This is an observation guide, not instruction in striking, wall escapes or submissions against strikes.

start_here.title: Annotate what changes around a familiar position
start_here.task: Choose an MMA round you can review and isolate a grappling exchange. Make separate notes for positional changes, offensive actions and use of the fence. Compare the notes with the scoring clarification’s distinction between offense and holding. If grounded status or a fence grip matters, consult the relevant foul provision and the event’s adopted rules before labeling the action legal or illegal.
start_here.section: ABC clarification: Dominance and Successful Grappling. Unified Rules: fouls 12–15.

flashcards.question: In the ABC’s July 2025 MMA judging clarification, does merely holding a dominant position establish dominance?
flashcards.answer: No. The clarification distinguishes static holding from positional offense that continually forces defense against potentially fight-ending attacks.
